blocks.text: Real-world analogue: A survey cairn on an open plateau, a desert geodetic marker, a sparse stone circle, a navigational beacon, and a dry rock garden whose few elements make orientation unmistakable.
World relation: Continuity establishes the return point; Pilgrim practice gives that point meaning by leaving and coming back changed.

Connection to newer locations: The First Place can serve as the conceptual opposite of the Plain of Missing Distance and the Valley That Restores Wrong. It can also be the oldest stable marker used by travelers from Doorway Plaza or the Stair of Thin Air.
Abstract or metaphorical relation: A place begins when more than one being agrees that return is possible. Its importance comes from shared orientation, not ornament or size.
